div.l: His tithis payd he fulle feir͗e and welle
Both in his ꝓpropre swinke and his catelle ·
In a tabard he rode vpon̄ a Mere
¶ Ther was also a Reve and a Miller͗e
A Sıı̄unnour and a pardoner also
A Maunciple and myselue ther wer͗e no mo
The Miller was a stout cherle for the nones
Ful bigge he was of brawne and eke of bones
That proued wel / for euer ther he cam̄
At wrestling he wold haue alwey the game
He was short shuldird and brood a thik carre .
Ther nas no dore that he nold heve of barre
Or breke it at a rennyng with his hede
His berd as any Sowe or Fox was rede ·
And therto brood as it were a Spade
Vpon the coppe Ryght of his nose he hade ·
A wert / and theron stode a tufte of heris
Rede as burstils of a Sowes erys
His nosethirles were blac and wyde .
A Swerd and a bokeler bare he be his side
His mouthe as gret was as a gret fourneys
He was a Iangler as golyardeys ·
And that was most of synne and harlotryes ·
Wel coude he stele corne and tolle thryes
And yit he had a thumbe of gold parde
White cote and a blue hood wered he
A bagpipe wel couth he blowe ⁊and sovn̄
And therwithal he brought vs out of tovn̄
¶ A gentle Maunciple was ther of a Temple
Of whom alle Catours might take exemple
Forto be wise in bying of vitayles
For whethir that he paide or toke by tailes
Algate he waytid so in his acate
That he was ay before and in good state
Now is nat that of god a fulle gret grace
That such a lewde mannes witte shal pas
The wisdom̄ of an hepe of lerned men̄
Of maistirs had he mo than thries tenne
That were of lawe expert and curious ·
Of which ther were a doseyn̄ in an house
